'''Sterling Brown''' (born February 10, 1995) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for [[Southern Methodist University]] (SMU), wrapping up his career in 2017.

==High school and college career==
Brown played high school basketball at [[Proviso East High School]] in [[Maywood, Illinois]]. Playing for coach [[Donnie Boyce]], he led the Pirates to a state runner-up finish in 2012 and a state semifinal appearance in 2013, losing both times to the [[Jabari Parker]]-led [[Simeon Career Academy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/blog/chicago/high-school/post/_/id/2829/simeon-sets-state-record-with-sixth-title|title=Simeon sets state record with sixth title|accessdate=June 20, 2017|date=March 18, 2012|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Powers, Scott}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://blogs.pjstar.com/eye/2013/03/15/chicago-simeon-wins-their-class-4a-state-semifinal-68-56-over-proviso-east/|title=Chicago Simeon Wins Their Class 4A State Semifinal, 68-56 Over Proviso East|accessdate=June 20, 2017|date=March 15, 2013|work=[[Peoria Journal Star]]}}</ref> Brown ultimately selected [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]] and coach [[Larry Brown (basketball)|Larry Brown]] over [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]], [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]] and [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]].<ref name=TSN>{{cite news|last1=|first1=|title=SMU lands Shannon Brown's brother, Sterling |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/news/4269534-smu-lands-shannon-browns-brother-sterling|accessdate=June 17, 2017|work=[[Sporting News]]|date=October 16, 2012}}</ref>

Brown and the Mustang class of 2017 endured three years of adversity as they missed the [[NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]] in his freshman season, then were upset the following season. In his junior year, SMU served an NCAA probation in [[2015–16 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2015–16]].<ref name="Endured">{{cite news|last1=Baby|first1=Ben|title=After so much adversity, SMU seniors Moore, Brown, Wilfong out to exit on high note |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/college-sports/smumustangs/2017/03/03/much-adversity-smu-seniors-moore-brown-wilfong-exit-high-note|accessdate=June 17, 2017|work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|date=March 3, 2017}}</ref> In his senior season, Brown averaged 13.4 points and 6.5 rebounds per game. Along with [[Semi Ojeleye]] he led the Mustangs to a 30–5 record and regular-season and Tournament [[American Athletic Conference]] championships. At the close of the season, Brown was named second-team All-conference.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Baby|first1=Ben|title=Semi Ojeleye leads four SMU players named to All-AAC teams |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/college-sports/smumustangs/2017/03/07/semi-ojeleye-leads-four-smu-players-named-aac-teams|accessdate=June 17, 2017|work=[[The Dallas Morning News]]|date=March 7, 2017}}</ref> Brown finished his Mustang career as the school's all-time leader in wins.<ref name="Endured"/>

==Professional career==
Following the close of his college career, Brown raised his profile by appearing in the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] College All-Star game and attended the [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament]]. He is considered a potential second-round prospect for the [[2017 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=|first1=|title=Rosters Announced for Reese's Division I All-Star Game |url=http://www.nabc.org/NABC_Releases/2017/d1_asg_roster|accessdate=June 17, 2017|work=[[National Association of Basketball Coaches]]|date=March 28, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Faigan|first1=Harrison|title=Shannon Brown's brother Sterling goes from watching Lakers' titles to working out for LA |url=https://www.silverscreenandroll.com/2017/5/30/15716836/la-lakers-shannon-brown-brother-sterling-workout-stats-draftexpress|accessdate=June 17, 2017|work=[[SBNation.com]]|date=May 30, 2017}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Brown is the younger brother of former NBA player [[Shannon Brown]]. Both brothers played for coach Larry Brown – Shannon with the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] and Sterling at SMU.<ref name=TSN/>
